quest.title: The Children of Vimara Village
quest.description: The woman who goes by the name of Rana seems to be a Forest Watcher of Sumeru. Accept her invitation and travel to Vimara Village.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x25000, Hero's Wit x3

talks.objective: Talk to Rana once you are ready

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: When you're ready, I'll take you to Vimara Village. It's smooth sailing from there to either Sumeru City or Port Ormos.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: I'm a Forest Watcher, after all. Escorting travelers is my job.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay, follow me!

choices.text: I've got something else on the table right now.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: All right. Be safe.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: It's only been a few days and a new Withering Zone has popped up already. So close to the main road, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Withering Zone again...

choices.text: We handled one with Tighnari before.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Tighnari disposed of a Withering Zone before? I won't go into how dangerous it is, then.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Regardless, lemme mark down the location and radius of effect for now. After I take you to Vimara Village, I'll go to Gandharva Ville and bring Tighnari over to help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No need, Rana, just leave it to us.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: No way! The Withering Zone is lethal, even veteran Forest Watchers wouldn't approach it unless absolutely necessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME} can manipulate the elements, and it should somewhat stave off the Withering's effects!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Eh? Now that I think about it, you did show such ability when fending off the Fungi...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: But still, you shouldn't do that. We can't have you injured by the Withering after coming all this way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't worry, Rana! {NICKNAME} has proven to be very reliable in the many encounters throughout our journey.

choices.text: Leave it to me. It's a piece of cake.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: *sigh* All right, I understand. I'll wait here. If it's too much to handle, get out of there or call for help, and I'll be there.

choices.text: I don't like this Withering Zone. Let me deal with it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, we cleared a Withering Zone with Tighnari before. Paimon recalls that was near Gandharva Ville, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} is impressive, right?

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: You're amazing! Incredibly amazing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're getting too excited, Rana.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #Pardon me... Ahem, {NICKNAME}... Uh, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss}...

choices.text: You don't have to be so formal...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay... So, I wonder if you guys are interested in joining us? I can vouch for you both.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #It would be great to get powerful, dedicated people like {NICKNAME} and Paimon on our side!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: With you guys, we can better control the spread of The Withering... Sure, you're probably not familiar with the woods, but that shouldn't be too much of a problem...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah, speaking of the forest, Paimon's got a question...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you remember the wondrous creatures we saw before?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Wondrous creatures...?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You quickly describe the wondrous creatures you met previously.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Oh, they sound like the mythical Aranara! Small, round, plantlike fairies. They are denizens of the woods and guardians of trees.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #But we generally dismiss them as just a tale. You sure those weren't just some Shroomboars you saw, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shroomboars?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Yeah, that's an animal you'll see only in the forests of Sumeru! They are round, green beasts that live in the forest. We'd use them to find precious mushrooms.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Anyway, in all my years in the woods, I've never seen an Aranara.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: However, you can ask the kids after you get to Vimara Village. They seem to be very into the legend of Aranara.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Although children always try to hide their thoughts from adults, you can read their minds like a book.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just like Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, that's because we're buddies and know each other very well!

choices.text: I don't think they're the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like we can probably make a stew with mushrooms out of them! Though Paimon doesn't think that's quite the same thing as what we saw...

choices.text: It's okay to just speak your mind, Miss Rana.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Let's drop the formalities, {NICKNAME} and Rana!

dialogues.speaker: Iosaphat
dialogues.text: It's you! Welcome. Come over for a meal with Rana and the cubs if you get a chance. Got a nice catch today.

talks.objective: Talk to the elders in the village

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: I'm back, Grandpa Amadhiah!

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Rana! You know, the job of a Forest Watcher is important, but you should come around more often.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Yeah, I know. I patrol the forest so that those "tiger cubs" can hang out in the woods safely. It was just a mess right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are tigers in Vimara Village?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: "Tiger cubs" refers to Iotham and his friends. By the way, your voice... I don't think I've ever met you. Do we have visitors?

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Oh, yes, Grandpa Amadhiah. These two are...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Rana gives Amadhiah a brief rundown.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. Welcome to Vimara Village, and thanks for helping Rana out.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: I plan to form a nightwatch, getting Alphonso, Bahram, and Aurelius to safeguard the perimeter as a group.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: That's a great plan. It's for the good of the children, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Has something happened in Vimara Village lately?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Could it be related to the round plantlike creatures we saw before?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? That sounded like a cabbage from your description.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: It's okay. We're just a little uneasy from some recent events.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: I've spent my whole life in Vimara Village and never saw anything like this. *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: I won't bore you with my stories. Please watch over Rana. She's always been a troublemaker since she was little.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: She got lost in the woods once when she was seven or eight, for a couple of days...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Hey now, Grandpa Amadhiah!

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Fine, fine. You be a good host now, Rana. Don't let our guests down.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: For sure!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce these two impressive travelers who have helped me a lot. And this here is Alphonso, just about the most dependable person in Vimara Village!

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: You flatter me, Rana. Anyway, nice to meet you two, and thanks for looking after Rana.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't look like a local, Alphonso. Are you a traveler, too?

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: Hahaha, you're an experienced traveler indeed, saw right through me at a glance.

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: I came as an apprentice from Fontaine, but ended up staying because I really like it here.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: And it's been years since! Alphonso is practically one of us now!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Anyway, how are the kids? They're not running around, are they? I mean, it's not a good time right now...

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: They're in the village, waiting for you to return. After Kavus came back...

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: Is it really okay to talk about that in front of our guests? Maybe we should talk about it later...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it something important? We can come back later...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Don't worry. They saved my life, after all!

choices.text: Actually, you could've made it on your own...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Time is life to me. You saved me time, so you saved my life!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Anyway, some of the children in Vimara Village have gone missing recently.

choices.text: That warrants much more than just an "Anyway"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is a very serious problem! Have you notified the sheriff in Sumeru City yet? Is there anything we can help with?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Wait, wait, just listen to me! The missing children always came back in a few days, though they don't remember what happened.

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: I'd round up a search party every time. Sometimes, we'd run into wild animals, sometimes a Withering Zone, other times, outsiders obviously too tough for us to handle.

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: However, we could never find the kids since the woods are simply too big to search, even for Rana.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Yeah, but in the end they would suddenly return when no one was paying attention, and couldn't recall anything when asked.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Whoa, so it's normal for kids?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, quit it, you two!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Hahahaha! Sorry to digress.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They remembered nothing at all?

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: I'm not sure. I think they just don't want to tell us "adults."

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: *sigh* Even though I'm only a few years older than them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, that's pretty concerning.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Right, so I've been patrolling nearby recently, looking out for anything unusual. That's also why I just spoke to Amadhiah about forming a nightwatch.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I also asked Alphonso to keep an eye on the kids...

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: Sorry.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: It's okay. I'd be more concerned if they actually stay put!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I'm going to have a word with Iosaphat later. It's his job to watch after Kavus and Sudabeh!

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: You ought to take it easy for a while here, Rana. You're the only one who can get through to the kids.

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: It's dangerous outside lately. Withering Zone aside, you got the Fatui from Snezhnaya with their armed mercenaries operating in the forest. If something goes wrong...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Fatui?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I know, I'll be careful, but I should be on the ball because it is dangerous!

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: But even if you could deal with the wild animals, the Fatui are more than you can handle, Rana.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds like Alphonso knows the Fatui very well.

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: Oh, I learned about them from the travelers shuttling between Sumeru City and Port Ormos.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: It's Rana! Rana is back! With Alphonso too!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Hee, here comes trouble!

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: Anyway, think it over, Rana.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: I picked a bunch of Starshrooms for you, Rana!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Iotham, didn't you promise me to never wander outside the village? The Rishboland Raja will come and get you if you don't behave!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: I'm big now and I'm not scared of anything!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Did you catch the Gator Raja this time, Rana?

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: I want to hear some tales from the woods, Rana!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Well, I didn't see the Gator Raja this time, but I brought you a golden lion and a silver...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Silver what, though...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aroo! Hehe, our colors match pretty well.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Silver Dusk Bird!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Silver Bass!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Super Silver Specter!

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: #All right, stop picking on them. {NICKNAME} and Paimon are my friends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *exhale* Paimon's not going to get mad at kids... Regardless, you know a lot of animals!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: That's right! Rana would tell us stories every time she's back. She told us about a huge, huge gator last time, and the Sumpter Beastlord!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: And the Rishboland Raja that couldn't be caught!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: That's right, and it will come and get you if you don't behave!

response.speaker: Children
response.text: Oh no!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Everyone in the village sure seems to get along!)

choices.text: (If only it could always be like this...)

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Anyway, my friends here came from a place far far away! Why don't we let them tell a story today?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, our trip to Sumeru has been a very eventful one!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Yay! Let's all go to Rana's house!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: The last one there is a Specter!

response.speaker: Alphonso
response.text: Be careful going over the bridge, don't fall into the water!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Let's go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why Weasel Thief!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What does Paimon have to do with Whopperflower!?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Yes, very impressive!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon thinks you're a good enough fighter to get it done yourself. Paimon means, don't you run into wild animals a lot as a Forest Watcher?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: That is true. However, time is life to me. You saved me time, so you saved my life.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Ah, friends of Rana, sorry about before. I must apologize for my aging eyes.

choices.text: About the mysterious creatures we saw before...

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: You mean the round little plantlike fairies? I think I saw them before, but when and what was it...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are they called Aranara?

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Aranara... Probably. I might have heard stories before, but I'm too old to remember for sure.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: The forests of Sumeru are very big, teeming with countless wondrous creatures. But one won't miss what they're destined to find.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: However, if I was destined, I shouldn't have forgotten about them, either. So when was it...?

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Rana is a good kid. She works hard every day to keep this old man and the children in Vimara Village safe.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: I wonder when she'll have time to start a family and settle down.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Okay, goodbye.

talks.objective: Follow the children to Rana's house

dialogues.speaker: Iotham
dialogues.text: I want dragon stories! Alphonso told me they exist in the world! He said a huge, evil dragon lives in a place called Mondstadt!

choices.text: Alphonso sure has his ears on the ground.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we know about that!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: So what is that dragon like? Alphonso said it is terrifying and pillages Mondstadt!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... How should Paimon put it?

choices.text: "This is a tale of friends resolving their misunderstanding..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem, here it goes: A long, long time ago, in a kingdom faraway, a big dragon with huge wings and sharp fangs laid in deep slumber.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text:
"When the dragon woke up, it saw the world had changed."
"Growl!" The dragon announced. "I'm mad now and I'm going to wreck your little houses and keeps!"
"The dragon wasn't actually bad but was tricked by an evil sorcerer into thinking everyone's bad."
"Then one day, two travelers arrived..."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon tells the story of the azure-blue dragon in a way that really engages the kids.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So, with everyone's help, the travelers removed the curse from the dragon and helped it find its friend.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Wow, I had thought dragons were terrible and would eat Sumpter Beasts and people!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: How big is the dragon, though? Big like a house?

choices.text: Big enough to swallow Paimon in one bite.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: If Paimon is the white lady? I guess the dragon isn't that big, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Paimon might be short, but she's got a big brain!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And a big appetite too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, Paimon can swallow the whole Vimara Village in one bite, just like the dragon!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Wow! If that's true, we can fly around inside a dragon's belly!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: When it gets hot, we'll go to the Snezhnaya that Alphonso talked about, where it snows! When it's rainy season, we'll go to Valuka, where Granny Jehiet is from!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Valuka?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Oh, that's a desert! Anyway, when I grow up, I want to travel everywhere like you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Travel and make friends. Just like how we traveled and got to know you! Can we ask you a few questions, Iotham?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ask about the mysterious creatures in the forest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rana told us they could be Aranara. Have you heard anything about them, Iotham?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Uh, about that...

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: No, I heard nothing about Aranara.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: On second thought, yeah, they do! Hahaha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? So you've seen Aranara before?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Actually, I've heard about them in Granny Jehiet's stories!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: No...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All right, we'll drop it. Rana and others are very worried about you kids, Iotham. Have you gotten lost in the woods recently?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: No, I know the woods very well. There's no way I can get lost!

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: But Sudabeh and Kavus did. Everyone was worried, but not me, because I know Arana would take them home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Arana? Who's that?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Uh, I mean Rana! Rana would find them and take them home!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (That's suspicious, but Paimon doesn't think we can find out more...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's change the topic! Why are you interested in dragon stories, Iotham?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: I want to be great like a dragon, then I can help Rana and Alphonso. They work very hard. It always takes a long time for Rana to patrol the woods.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Alphonso goes out there when no one's looking too. I can help them as soon as I grow up, so they can spend more time in the village.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it! You're a great kid, Iotham!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rana and others are very worried about you kids, Iotham. Have you gotten lost in the woods recently?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Hahaha! No, they don't!

choices.text: Big enough to swallow Vimara Village in one bite.
"This is a tale of heroes triumphing over evil..."

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: It's only been a few days and a new Withering Zone has popped up already. So close to the main road, too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Withering Zone?

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Oh, that's a "disaster" unique to Sumeru. It's a force that emerges in an area and kills all living things within.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's true, all of the plants died.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Yeah. Tighnari would be able to eliminate it if he was around. But for someone like me, who doesn't have a Vision and cannot control the elements, it's very dangerous to go into a Withering Zone.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Regardless, lemme mark down the location and radius of effect for now. After I take you to Vimara Village, I'll go to Gandharva Ville and bring Tighnari over to help.

choices.text: Great, I don't have a Vision.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But can't you control the elements? What was it? Oh yeah, "Prepare to be blown away!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since you can control the elements, you should be able to help!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Eh? Now that I think about it, you did show such ability when fending off the Fungi...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: But we still shouldn't try. Withering Zones are lethal, and even veteran Forest Watchers wouldn't approach one unless absolutely necessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That might be the case, but {NICKNAME} has proven to be very reliable in the many encounters throughout our journey.

choices.text: Leave it to me. It's a piece of cake.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: *sigh* All right, I understand. I'll wait here. If it's too much to handle, get out of there or call for help, and I'll be there.

choices.text: I don't like this Withering Zone. Let me deal with it.
It's tough being a Forest Watcher.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But can't you control the elements? What was it? Oh yeah, "Prepare to be blown away!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should help!

talks.objective: Follow the children to Rana's house

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These kids ran faster than birds could fly...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: You guys are getting good at running. It's going to worry me sick if you run away someday.

dialogues.speaker: Iotham
dialogues.text: We won't run if Rana's here!

dialogues.speaker: Sudabeh
dialogues.text: I'm going to marry Rana when I grow up!

dialogues.speaker: Kavus
dialogues.text: Wait, didn't you promise to marry me? Liar!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Hahaha, we'll sort this out later! You'll meet more people when you grow up, people more impressive and better than me.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #For instance, {M#Mr. Blond}{F#Miss Blonde} here is way mightier than me, and has met many great people along their journey from far away, right?

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Have you been traveling a long time?

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Rana said you'd tell us stories!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #You got the tiger cubs, then. I have a meeting to go to. You kids be good to {M#him}{F#her} and stay put till I come back.

response.speaker: Children
response.text: Okay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All right, on to the stories... You're Iotham, right? What story would you like to hear?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Stories about dragons! Alphonso said they are ancient and very powerful!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Sea monsters! I heard there's a lot of big monsters in the sea!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: I want stories about a distinguished lady who is smart and powerful!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: #{M#I want to be like Rana when I grow up, so I want to hear stories like that!}{F#Yeah, you are powerful, and very pretty too! But I'm going to be Rana's bride, so I have to be stronger than you!}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They all want different stories...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey... Isn't there someone that knows stories of the eight-headed hydras, silver-haired banshees, and the wicked abyss dragon? Paimon thinks everyone would be happy if that person was here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How about this, we know a lot of stories, and we'll tell them all!

choices.text: (We can ask them about the mysterious creatures while at it.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (True, these kids might know things adults don't, and about how they went missing...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As a trade, Iotham, Kavus, and Sudabeh, you'll tell us what you know too.

response.speaker: Children
response.text: Sure!

choices.text: (We can ask them about how they went missing while at it.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (True! And about the mysterious creatures too.)

choices.text: I've got a lot of stories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Kavus
dialogues.text: Sea monsters! I heard there's a lot of big and peculiar monsters in the sea!

dialogues.speaker: Kavus
dialogues.text: Like the fish that's as large as an island, or the squid as long as a river, and the story about the puppet and the whale! Also, the turtle carrying an elephant on its back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've heard a lot of stories! Why the interest in sea monsters?

dialogues.speaker: Kavus
dialogues.text: When I grow up, I want to be a sailor, going on seven voyages and discovering uncharted islands and lands! That's why I want to learn about sea monsters. This way, I can defeat them one day!

choices.text: We ran across some pirates before.

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Wow! That's so cool! Did they find any treasure? Any tales of adventure?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not sure, but Paimon does have a sea-monster story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem. Once upon a time, there was a sea serpent with many heads living in the ocean! It was taller than a mountain when it stretched out its neck...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text:
"The serpent didn't behave, so a god trapped it on the sea floor under rocks to prevent it from making waves and destroying the harbor."
"After a long while, the serpent woke up and griped, 'Curse you, despicable god!'"
"'I'll wash all your houses and treasures out to the sea and make them mine! Roar!'"
"Then it rose up to higher than the mountains and caused a tidal wave..."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon tells the story of the people in the flying castle fighting the sea hydra together in a way that really engages the kids.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And that was how everybody worked together to defeat the serpent and protect the city!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: So the serpent has been defeated? What a shame, I wanted to beat it myself when I grew up!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Of course! I'm older than Iotham and Sudar, I have to be stronger than them so I can protect them.

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: I promised to tell you what I know after hearing your story. So, what would you like to know?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About the mysterious creatures in the woods...

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Oh, there's a lot of them in the forest! Like the legendary Sumpter Beastlord — it isn't like any ordinary Sumpter Beast and will attack intruders!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: And the Rishboland Raja that snatches bad children away! But I'm old enough to know Rana made that up to scare the kids.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They all sound interesting, but we'd like to know about the round, plantlike fairies called Aranara. Do you know about them?

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Oh, Aranara...

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Never heard of them, but I know about the Gator Raja! It's a very, very big gator in the woods that has lived for a long, long time and is very, very cunning. There was this one time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (That didn't sound convincing...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Paimon can't believe there's a gator like that! Do you go into the woods often, Kavus?

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Yeah, I used to, but not lately, since I got lost in there once. At least that's what the adults said.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "That's what the adults said?"

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Because I don't remember anything. I went into the forest to see my friend and share stories about my sister, then... I just can't remember what happened.

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: When I came to my senses, I was back in the village already. My father held me tightly while everyone was around me, asking me if I was hurt, hungry, or thirsty. Then they wouldn't let me go there again.

choices.text: You should listen and not go there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm... But you have a friend in the forest? Doesn't everyone live in the village?

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Yeah, a friend to everyone, lives in the forest. Taught us many things, like what wild fruits we shouldn't eat, and which trees would let us climb on them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm, so what is that friend like?

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Well...

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: I can't tell you. I'm sorry. Although we're friends, I made a pact with Sudabeh and Iotham.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Paimon guesses it's a secret between the kids...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I think we just hit a dead end.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, we understand. Now, be a good boy and don't play outside the village!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Of course! I'll be a good big brother to Sudabeh and Iotham!

choices.text: You went into the forest to see your friend?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You have a friend in the forest? Doesn't everyone live in the village?

choices.text: You'll face other "monsters" when you grow up.

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: What kind of monsters?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's talk about something else...

choices.text: We ran across the grandson of some pirate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What story would you like to hear, Sudabeh?

dialogues.speaker: Sudabeh
dialogues.text: Any story will do! But I'd like it to have a distinguished lady who is smart and powerful. Well, she doesn't have to be a distinguished lady, but the character's got to be determined and loving.

dialogues.speaker: Sudabeh
dialogues.text: Like Princess Cinnamon who left her palace with a tiger in the fairytale!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a lot of demands...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon knows several ladies who fit that description, but somehow they all have connections to Electro...

dialogues.speaker: Sudabeh
dialogues.text: Electro is good. It makes plants stronger and bear more fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know a lot, Sudabeh! So, where should Paimon start...

choices.text: "In a place far away, there was a library..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can go with the story of Miss Lisa, but Paimon'd prefer another one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem. In a place far away, on the other side of the ocean, there was a lady general and a shrine maiden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, making the shrine maiden a priestess, and the general a queen should help you understand it better.

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Are they both distinguished ladies?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, they both are!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "Once upon a time, in a kingdom far away, there was a very beautiful and powerful queen. But war came, and although the queen won, she also lost many friends."\n"She cried and cried, '*sob* I'm going to make a robot and have it work for me. Then I shall live alone in the palace forever and not make any more friends so I won't lose them!'"\n"'Beep. Copy that. Working now,' replied the robot, who then began running the kingdom for the queen. Then some bad guys started to scheme!"

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Where does the priestess come in?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: #"Ahem. The queen had a pretty and powerful priestess friend, who couldn't bear to see the queen go on this way."\n"That was when a traveler came to the kingdom. {M#He}{F#She} and {M#his}{F#her} companion were both smart and brave."\n"So the priestess thought, 'Ack-ack-ack! They are agile and resilient. If they're willing to help...'"

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon tells the story of the queen and the priestess (both of whom are distinguished ladies) in a way that really engages the kids.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...In the end, the lonely robot was still working hard, but that's another story.

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: #Everyone was so awesome! Even though that traveler wasn't a distinguished lady, {F#she}{M#he} was still strong. That's what I want to be when I grow up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's sure you can do it! But if you don't behave and get lost out there, then none of that will happen!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Yes, I'll behave and won't wander outside.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What happened when you got lost before?

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: I don't remember. I just went into the woods to gather herbs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Herbs?

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Yeah. Alphonso said there's a herb to improve grandpa's eyesight. He has trouble seeing things lately and can't even see people coming his way. So I wanted to help grandpa.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did Alphonso send you?

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: No. He warned me not to wander into the forest too, but I wanted to help, so I sneaked off. Then I don't remember the rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nothing at all?

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Nothing. When I came round, I was already home. My brother said everyone was worried. I know what I did was wrong and will never sneak off into the woods again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, good girl. Speaking of the forest...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About the mysterious creatures in the woods...

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: I don't know anything about them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that was fast!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: What do you mean by "mysterious"? If I know what they are, they're not mysterious. If I don't, I wouldn't be able to tell you. Sorry...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That actually makes a lot of sense... But what Paimon wanted to ask about is round, plantlike fairies...

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Round and plantlike... Oh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did that ring a bell, Sudabeh?

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Uh, no! That sounds mysterious!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... That's a shame, because Rana said she would love to know what an Aranara is!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Oh, she wants to know too? Then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She does! Also, didn't the priestess in the story say, "Ack-ack-ack! Don't be a tantrum-throwing child who refuses to talk to others!"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Ack-ack-ack!"

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Okay... The priestess and the queen are really great friends.

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: But like how they trust each other, I think Rana would understand why I can't say it.

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: When I'm old enough to understand a lot more, I'll tell Rana and you two. But no, not now.

choices.text: Well, I hope you can grow up healthy and happy.

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Thanks!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then, we won't ask more questions. Just be a good girl and don't wander around.

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Mm-hmm! Thank you for the story, I love it very much. I'm going to be smart, pretty, and strong just like the priestess!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: Then I'll marry Rana!

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: It's okay. I'll also age, so you'll always be more mature than me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* It seems they know about the mysterious creatures but just don't want to tell us...

choices.text: Should we divide and conquer them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, they're kids, not villains! Just treat it as a secret they don't want the adults to know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're staying in Sumeru for a while and will have time to look into it.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I'm back! How did it go? Was it fun?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: It was fun! They told us a story. Dragons actually don't eat people, Rana!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Oh yeah? That's good to hear. I was worried a dragon might fly over here and eat you all some day!

response.speaker: Children
response.text: Oh no!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Storytelling is kinda fun!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay, you should go home now. It's about time to eat. Iosaphat said he caught good stuff in the water today!

response.speaker: Kavus
response.text: Come with us, Rana! And both of you too!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: We've got business to tend to, but thanks for the invite.

response.speaker: Sudabeh
response.text: I want to eat with Rana...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I'll be there next time! Come on, you've got to go now or Iosaphat is going to finish it all by himself!

response.speaker: Children
response.text: Okay! Bye, Rana, bye, you two!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Stick around for a minute, Iotham. I want to talk to you.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I'm concerned about you. The forest hasn't been the same lately. The animals are getting aggressive and more Fungi have popped up. Same with the Withering Zones, which keep appearing.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Don't go picking mushrooms anymore, okay, Iotham?

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Don't worry, I know where's safe and not safe. What's more, Starshrooms are tasty, and they give you the energy to keep working hard.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: No, Granny Jehiet and I are both worried. Promise me that you won't run around out there before I figure out what's going on.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Okay...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: That's a good boy, Iotham. You'll be great when you grow up. All right, go eat with Kavus and others.

response.speaker: Iotham
response.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I hope they'll grow up safe and sound.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #What do you think about these kids, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Yeah, I understand. Regardless, I hope they'll grow up safe and sound.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: My patrol is actually not done yet. I've still got to check out the west, and...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #And I have a favor to ask. {NICKNAME} and Paimon, would you mind coming with me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Why?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #I spotted some Withering Zones there with no one to check them. I'm very worried about kids wandering into one. {NICKNAME}, now that you're here, will you give me a hand with that?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Please, though I have nothing to repay you with...

choices.text: I'll take that nice axe of yours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! {M#He}{F#She} is only joking. We don't need payment, right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: So you will help? I really appreciate it! I don't know how I can make it up to you. You've done so much for me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we're not going to ignore those in need.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Mm! Let's go, then!

choices.text: We have nothing else to do anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll just call it exercising!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Is that supposed to be a compliment?

choices.text: Should we get the adults in town to pressure them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, they're kids, not villains! Just treat it as a secret they don't want the adults to know.

choices.text: Just treat it as a secret between these kids.

talks.objective: Leave Vimara Village and go to the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Sudabeh
dialogues.text: When I grow up, I want to be strong, smart, very pretty, and take Rana as my bride.

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: The mission... I don't want to do it... What should I do? If the kids... Rana...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let's leave quietly.)

dialogues.speaker: Jehiet
dialogues.text: Hey, it's the visitor Rana brought. Welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Jehiet
dialogues.text: We don't have much in the village except a quiet life, so put your feet up and relax.

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: Welcome. The kids are excited to see visitors too.

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: #Welcome to Vimara Village, {NICKNAME}. Everyone is family here. If you stay, Iotham and his friends will treat you like a real {M#brother}{F#sister}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you know my name?

dialogues.speaker: Alphonso
dialogues.text: Rana probably mentioned it. Anyway, hope you'll enjoy your time in Vimara Village.

dialogues.speaker: Iotham
dialogues.text: So dragons don't eat people or Sumpter Beasts! I have to let Alphonso know next time.

dialogues.speaker: Kavus
dialogues.text: When I grow up, I want to be a great sailor like Sinbadacus!

dialogues.speaker: Sudabeh
dialogues.text: When I grow up, I want to be strong, smart, very pretty, and take Rana as my bride.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's go whenever you are ready!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Sure! It's not far to the west.

choices.text: I need to take care of some things first.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay. Give me a shout when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: The best thing about my house is that I can sneak out of it without anyone noticing. That's how I've been running off all the time since I was a kid.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Alright, back to business. {NICKNAME}, let's go whenever you are ready!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Sure! It's not far to the west.

choices.text: I need to take care of some things first.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay. Give me a shout when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, let's go whenever you are ready!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Sure! It's not far to the west.

choices.text: I need to take care of some things first.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay. Give me a shout when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I'll wait here. If it's too much to handle, get out of there or call for help, and I'll be there.
